translationRepairs: s0023 idiomatic ends with an extra closing quote after replied; 忠良對曰：「濟。」 supports the dialogue and speaker tag without that stray mark.
"Your Majesty will soon recover," Zhongliang answered."
"Your Majesty will soon recover," Zhongliang answered.
s0040 idiomatic likewise has a stray closing quote after answered; 忠良對曰：「聖體行自安矣。」 is a single reply that needs only one closing quote on the speech.
"The omen concerns the Heir Apparent," Zhongliang replied."
"The omen concerns the Heir Apparent," Zhongliang replied.
s0056 idiomatic has the same stray closing quote after replied; the Chinese is one speech attribution 忠良對曰：「應在皇太子宮矣。」

On the night of the fifteenth of the seventh month, a white comet streaked through the Three Terraces constellation. When the emperor asked what it portended, Zhongliang said, "Surely one of the Three Dukes is about to die!"

On the night of the fifteenth day of the seventh month, a white vapor pierced the Three Terraces. When the emperor asked what it portended, Zhongliang replied, "Might the Three Dukes be about to die?"
s0028 白氣貫三台 is a white vapor piercing the Three Terraces, not a comet, and 三公其死乎！ is a predictive question about the Three Dukes, not a claim that one of them will die.
When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Zhongliang was promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and received a silver seal.
When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Zhongliang was promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and Grand Minister of Education and received a silver seal.
s0080 大司徒 is Grand Minister of Education, not Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; drop the awkward parenthetical (dasitu) while keeping the correct office title.
When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Zhongliang was advanced to Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and granted a silver seal.
When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Zhongliang was advanced to Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and Grand Minister of Education, and granted a silver seal.
Literal s0080 likewise mistranslates 大司徒 as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; the proposed Grand Minister of Education matches the office.

When Emperor Chengzong led the imperial grandson to garrison the northern frontier, the court sent envoys to invest the heir with the imperial seal. Dejin accompanied the expedition, and in every battle won he predicted the day of victory in advance — and none failed to come true.

When Emperor Chengzong, as imperial grandson, garrisoned the northern frontier, the court sent envoys to invest the heir with the imperial seal. Dejin accompanied the expedition, and in every battle won he predicted the day of victory in advance — and none failed to come true.
成宗以皇孫撫軍北邊 marks Chengzong himself acting as imperial grandson when garrisoning the north, not leading another grandson.

Posthumously he was honored as meritorious minister who promoted loyalty and supported governance, grandee of glorious emolument, grand preceptor, pillar of state, and Duke of Wei, with the posthumous name Wenmu (Cultured and Solemn).

Posthumously he was honored as meritorious minister who promoted loyalty and supported governance, grandee of glorious emolument, grand minister of education, pillar of state, and Duke of Wei, with the posthumous name Wenmu (Cultured and Solemn).
s0284 大司徒 is Grand Minister of Education, not 太師/grand preceptor; lowercase the title to match the surrounding idiomatic title list.

Posthumously he was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promoted Loyalty and Supported Governance, Grandee of Glorious Emolument, Grand Preceptor, Pillar of State, and Duke of the State of Wei, with the posthumous name Wenmu.

Posthumously he was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promoted Loyalty and Supported Governance, Grandee of Glorious Emolument, Grand Minister of Education, Pillar of State, and Duke of the State of Wei, with the posthumous name Wenmu.
Literal s0284 likewise renders 大司徒 as Grand Preceptor; the proposed Grand Minister of Education is correct.

In 1281 Kang submitted a memorial: "In the year renpwu, Taiyi occupies the Gen Palace, with the Grand General as guest, the Deputy General imprisoned, and the Direct Talisman in charge of affairs — precisely the sphere of the Yan region.

In 1281 Kang submitted a memorial: "In the year renwu, Taiyi occupies the Gen Palace, with the Grand General as guest, the Deputy General imprisoned, and the Direct Talisman in charge of affairs — precisely the sphere of the Yan region.
歲壬午 romanizes as renwu; renpwu is a typographical error in the idiomatic field.

In the eighteenth year, Kang memorialized: "In the year renpwu, Taiyi governs the Gen Palace; the Grand General is guest, the Deputy General is imprisoned, and the Direct Talisman handles affairs — this directly corresponds to the Yan region.

In the eighteenth year, Kang memorialized: "In the year renwu, Taiyi governs the Gen Palace; the Grand General is guest, the Deputy General is imprisoned, and the Direct Talisman handles affairs — this directly corresponds to the Yan region.
Literal likewise misspells 壬午 as renpwu; renwu is the correct romanization.

During campaigns at Bin and Qian he charged into battle without flinching from arrows and stones. The emperor remonstrated with him, saying, "Even if you care nothing for your own life, have you no regard for the armor I depend on?"

During campaigns at Bin and Qian he charged into battle without flinching from arrows and stones. The emperor spoke solicitously to him, saying, "Even if you care nothing for your own life, have you no regard for the armor I depend on?"
帝勞之曰 marks solicitous concern/encouragement for the armorer, not remonstrance; the proposed wording restores that sense.
Administer medicines of cold blood, and the menses will flow."
Administer cold-natured blood-moving medicines, and the menses will flow."
寒血之藥 are cold-natured blood-moving medicines, not medicines of cold blood; the proposed literal matches the idiomatic sense and the Chinese.

In 1278 an edict restored him to lay dress; he was made grand master for splendid happiness and grand preceptor and placed in charge of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. In favor, rank, and reward none could compare with him.

In 1278 an edict restored him to lay dress; he was made grand master for splendid happiness and grand minister of education and placed in charge of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. In favor, rank, and reward none could compare with him.
s0254 大司徒 is Grand Minister of Education; 太師 appears only in the next unit's posthumous honors, so grand preceptor is wrong here.

In the fifteenth year an edict restored him to lay dress; he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor, and placed in charge of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. Favor, treatment, and rewards — none could be his equal.

In the fifteenth year an edict restored him to lay dress; he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Grand Minister of Education, and placed in charge of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. Favor, treatment, and rewards — none could be his equal.
Literal s0254 has the same 大司徒/太師 conflation; Grand Minister of Education is the correct office.

He had six sons. The first, Asengge, became grand minister of education;
